title_en: I Do Not Eat Spicy Food in Chinese

sentences.en: Today at noon, my colleague and I went to a restaurant together for lunch.
The waiter brought the menu and asked what dishes we wanted to eat.
My colleague loves spicy food, and he ordered an especially spicy dish.
I said, "I don't eat spicy food — you two order, I'll get something of my own."

t: to rest assured; not to worry
sentences.en: I asked the waiter: "Is this dish spicy?" The waiter said: "Not spicy — don't worry."
After the food arrived, my colleague drank water the whole time while eating.
My dish wasn't spicy at all — it was delicious, and I finished it all by myself.

vocab: to rest assured; not to worry

quiz.q: Why did the narrator ask the waiter if the dish was spicy?
a: Because the narrator can't eat spicy food

quiz.q: What did the colleague do while eating the spicy dish?
How was the narrator's own dish in the end?
a: Not spicy at all, and delicious

grammar.p: A不A？ (yes/no question with a repeated verb/adjective)
grammar.e: Repeating a verb or adjective with 不 in between makes a yes/no question, e.g. 辣不辣 'is it spicy or not.'
grammar.x: 这个菜辣不辣？— Is this dish spicy?

grammar.p: 一点儿都不 + adjective (not ... at all)
grammar.e: 一点儿都不 before an adjective emphasizes a complete absence of that quality.
grammar.x: 我的菜一点儿都不辣。— My dish wasn't spicy at all.

grammar.p: 一边 A，一边 B (to do A while doing B)
grammar.e: 一边 before two verb phrases shows both actions happening at the same time.
grammar.x: 同事一边吃，一边喝水。— My colleague drank water while eating.
